26232.description:
AUTO MOTIVE WORKSHOP MANAGER - LIHIR ISLAND
Responsibilities will include:
Inspecting vehicle and heavy trucks and machines engine and mechanical/electrical components to diagnose issues accurately and repair.
Inspecting vehicle computer and electronic systems to repair, maintain and or upgrade.
Develop and execute a routine maintenance schedule across the fleet.
Machines in our fleet include:- Diesel generators, heavy trucks, Wheel loader, Excavator, Screening plant, stacking plant, light Vehicles, light trucks and other small engine machines.
Inspect vehicle and machine engine and mechanical/electrical components to diagnose issues accurately AND REPAIR
Inspect vehicle computer and electronic systems to repair, maintain, upgrade and repair.
Be trained and experienced in petrol and diesel engine rebuilds and overhauls.
Be trained and experienced in fault diagnosis and repair of manual and automatic transmission of all kinds.
Requirements
Be an accomplished workshop manager who can run a small workshop and supervise and train local tradesmen and trades assistants to a high level of workmanship.
Proven experience as auto mechanic both in light vehicles and heavy equipment
Have good experience in hydraulic system in heavy equipment.
Excellent knowledge of mechanical, electrical and electronic and air driven components of light and heavy vehicles.
Be able computer literate and have the ability to source parts and problem solutions from suppliers and manufacturers on the internet.
Be able to set up and run a workshop assets/tools register and rigorously maintain it.
Be able to set up and execute a strong safety regimen within the work area.
Excellent physical condition.
High school diploma is preferred. Completion of Apprenticeship is essential with at least 10 years’ experience.
Extra-Curricular courses taken from machine suppliers will be highly considered.
Non-Smoking, Non- drinking, Quiet respectful person is sought.
Team Player with hands on mentality is essential.
Company will provide all PPE, Tools, Food, Medical and Laundry.
Sundays (or Saturday) depending on religious will be a non-workday.
Hours will be 9-hour days.
A police report and a medical certificate will be required.
References from former Employees/training institutions, course conductors etc. essential. These references must have contactable referees.
THIS POSITION IS OPEN TO PNG NATIONALS AND EXPATRIATES.
Job Location: Lihir Island. Papua New Guinea.
Renumeration
An Excellent competitive salary package will be offered to the person who can fit all the above requirements. Applicants can email their Applications in
zip file format
to:
[email protected]
Addressed to:
The Managing Director
Nica Limited
P.O. Box 113.
Lihir Island.
NIP.

25629.description:
Job Type:
Permanent
About us
K92 Mining Limited are the owners the high-grade Kainantu Gold Mine in Eastern Highlands Province. Since commencing operations in 2016, we have delivered consistent production growth. More importantly, we have contributed significantly to the economy of Papua New Guinea, more than 90% of our employees and contractors are from PNG and our local education and skills development initiatives which include scholarships, traineeships and adult literacy programs continue to bring significant benefit the communities in which we operate.
We are now transforming the operation with a new 1.2 mtpa process plant as well as extensive construction and expansion across site that will see us triple the output from our mine by 2027. In addition to our ongoing production success, we have an extensive exploration programme across our highly prospective tenement, making K92 a great place to build a long-term career.
About the role
In this role you will provide management and leadership within our mobile maintenance department. This rewarding role will see you provide daily mentoring, guidance, instruction, and training to the national workforce to increase safety performance, machinery uptime and efficient outcomes within a motivated and talented department.
Key Accountabilities
Coordinate workshop activities through the Mobile Maintenance Supervisors.
Give direction, delegate tasks and provide technical assistance to subordinates.
Liaise with senior maintenance leadership on planned maintenance.
Maintain stock levels and place orders as required.
Ensure cost control measures are considered by utilizing resources available to full capacity.
Report and rectify any hazardous sightings to the Mobile Maintenance Superintendent in the 800L workshop.
Ensure training requirements are met.
Organise and document weekly safety toolbox meetings workshop safety representatives.
Regularly monitors and evaluates staff performance in consultation with Mobile Maintenance Superintendent.
Provide coaching for performance improvement.
In conjunction with mobile maintenance superintendent, takes disciplinary action to address performance deficiencies, in accordance with the Company’s rules, policies and procedures.
Personally, responds to inquiries and complaints from the employees.
Responds to emergency situations as necessary.
Carry out other relative duties as directed by the Mobile Maintenance Superintendent.
Maintain safety work standards in accordance with government regulations and company policy.
Perform all roles and responsibilities that support and reflect the company’s mission and core values.
About You
Qualifications & Experience
Relevant trade qualification in Heavy Equipment Fitting, Auto Electrical and Automation. Minimum Certificate III required.
10+ years relevant work experience essential.
Underground mobile fleet such as Sandvik and Caterpillar and provide guidance of Methods, practices, techniques.
Ability to plan, assign, direct and coordinate a variety of functional specialties (areas) with overlapping work areas.
Must have at least 5 years in mobile fleet maintenance in a supervisory capacity. Should also have experience in training of both operating and maintenance personnel.
Experience in the use of Pronto will be advantageous.
Sound planning, analytical and problem-solving skills.
Excellent trouble shooting skills.
Self-motivated with the ability to work under pressure and autonomously.
Excellent attention to detail and time management skills to meet deadlines.
Strong active listening & interpersonal skills for rapport building, conflict resolution & training.
Actively promotes a safe and healthy culture.
Life at K92
K92 is an Equal Opportunity Employer, our commitment is to respect the rights of every individual to work to their highest potential, free from discrimination.  Our values of Collaboration, Accountability, Respect for others, Excellence and Safety are at the core of everything we do, and they are the foundation upon which our success has been built.
Our camp is well managed and provides residents with good, healthy meals made from locally sourced fresh produce as well as internet, cable tv and a gymnasium.
At K92, we want all employees to share in our success, so as well as a competitive salary, employees also participate in our long- and short-term incentive plans, we also provide employees with access to savings incentive programs, medical assistance and the option to salary sacrifice for certain expenses.
In addition to all of this, employees can also access our Wellbeing and employee assistance programs whilst working a friendly roster.
THIS POSITION IS OPEN ONLY TO CANDIDATES WHO HAVE THE RIGHT TO LIVE & WORK IN PNG WITHOUT SPONSORSHIP
Apply

26534.description:
Job Title:
Construction Site Engineer
Reports To:
Projects Manager
Department:
Campus and Facilities Management
Location:
IBSUniversity, Mt. Eriama, 11 Mile Campus
ORGANIZATIONAL CONTEXT:
The Institute of Business Studies (IBS) began its journey in 1987 as a modest initiative under Nades & Associates, primarily offering revision classes to support the needs of the Papua New Guinea Institute of Accountants, now known as CPA PNG. Over the past 36 years, IBS has grown steadily into a private university-level institution. Today, IBS is recognised as one of the largest business schools in Papua New Guinea, offering degree programmes in Accounting & Finance, Business & Management, Economics & Development Studies, and Information Technology. In addition, the institution continues to provide academic pathways for Grade 10 and 12 school leavers, as well as industry-recognised certification opportunities for experienced professionals seeking formal qualifications in their respective fields. This success has been made possible through the dedication and commitment of our team, whose collective efforts continue to make a meaningful contribution to Papua New Guinea by helping to educate and empower both current and future citizens.
A CAREER WITH US:
At IBS we believe that everyone has been gifted with natural talents and learnt skills. Our recruitment process is designed to help candidates understand this and enable us to better match you with a role that you will not only be able to do but enjoy doing. Career progression is also important to us and believes that each employee should be at the driving seat of their career progression - this means your manager will discuss with you where you want to be in the future and be more of a coach for you in terms of giving you feedback on areas you need to work on to be your best and achieve your goals. We also have a lot of staff events that enable us to celebrate as a team and give recognition where it's due.
ABOUT THIS ROLE:
Construction Site Engineer will be responsible for overseeing all the activities on the construction site. The Construction Site Engineer ensures that projects are completed on time, with a budget, and our client’s specifications. This includes planning, coordinating, and supervising onsite functions, staffing, scheduling, and material control.
KEY RESPONSIBILITIES:
Execution of site work – Directing, executing, consulting, monitoring, quality controlling, and punch listing (rectifications) of relevant Civil Engineering construction works including earthwork, drainage work, road construction, and building construction (concrete and steel) along with incidental construction (curb laying, paving Interlocking concrete blocks, etc.).
Workplace Communications- Methods applicable to target groups, providing specific information to workers about their safety and developing team performances, commitment, and corporation.
Technical supervision during construction - Assess performances according to approved plans and drawings and consult the manager/professionals for any predicted problems and changes in the ongoing construction.
Supervise construction projects to ensure they are completed in line with the scope, time, budget, and set quality standards.
Ensure all work complies with building codes and safety regulations.
Inspect project sites regularly to identify and eliminate potential safety hazards.
Supervising and instructing the construction team as well as subcontractors
Communicating with clients’ suppliers, and laborers effectively
Prepare and submit progress reports.
Ensuring the quality of materials and workmanship meet specified standards and codes.
Manage the procurement of materials, machinery, tools and equipment necessary for the project.
Resolving conflicts or miscommunication that may happen onsite quickly and amicably.
Education and Qualification
Bachelor’s degree in Civil Engineering, Construction Management, or a related field preferred.
Minimum of 5 years’ proven experience in a similar role.
In-depth knowledge of construction procedures, equipment, OSHA guidelines, and project management principles
Excellent organizational, leadership and management skills
Ability to communicate and report effectively.
Aptitude in Math and strong problem-solving skills
Good physical condition and stamina
Current state licensure for contacting or similar, if required
Exceptional attention to detail with an ability to spot potential risks or issues before they arise.
If interested, please submit your
updated CV with your supporting documents via the link below.
https://ibs.bamboohr.com/careers/172?source=aWQ9MTU%3D
Apply

26388.description:
Business Analyst
Simberi Gold Company Limited forms part of the St Barbara Group. Our Simberi Operations consists of an open cut mine on the northernmost island in the Tabar group of islands in the province of New Ireland in Papua New Guinea. Our vision is to grow sustainably and create enduring, positive impacts for the people and communities touched by our operations.
Now is an exciting time for our business and for our people. We’re going through a period of significant change and are gaining momentum in transforming our business. We’re looking for people who are ready to grow through opportunity and build a bright future with us.​​
We are currently seeking a
Business Analyst
to join our team. permanent full-time position at our Simberi Operation. Your work location is Papua New Guinea, working a 21/14 Roster from Kavieng, Rabaul, Port Moresby, Lae, Mt Hagen, Madang, Goroka, Alotau, Wapenamanda, Popondetta, Hoskins, Wewak, Vanimo, or Tabar group of Islands.
(
Locals are encouraged to apply)
.
Reporting to the Finance Superintendent, the successful candidate will provide finance and commercial support, analysis and governance to the Simberi Operation and projects
Everyone at St Barbara Limited is required to understand and act in accordance with St Barbara’s values and policies and meet all relevant internal and external compliance obligations. The role incumbent and manager will identify and review the specific compliance requirements of the role.
The Opportunity
Technical Accountabilities
Ensuring timely and accurate reporting, by proactively working with Managers and Superintendents to ensure reported results are accurate, including all necessary accruals and revaluations and that variances are adequately explained against budgets and forecasts.
Preparing and reviewing the annual budget and quarterly and ad-hoc forecasts under the supervision of the Senior Business Analyst.
Assist the Finance Superintendent and Accounting Supervisor in maintaining and updating the capital expenditure tracker for site-based projects, ensuring accuracy, timeliness, and alignment with budgetary controls
Leading a timely and accurate End of Month reporting process.
Ensuring all corporate reporting deadlines are met.
Working co-operatively and in conjunction with other Commercial department staff to ensure the best possible service to the operations.
Examine ways in which to improve both the service provided and the cost of the finance and admin functions.
Taking a proactive approach to problem-solving and continual organizational change through the identification and implementation of better ways to complete tasks.
Reviewing monthly variance analysis (actuals Vs forecast & financial year budget) and report to Simberi Management & Corporate Finance
Reviewing monthly costs, including cost initiatives to reduce, where possible, costs
Providing finance business partnering to Simberi operations and projects
Addressing outstanding audit issues to a “satisfactory” conclusion.
Scheduling accountabilities
Ensure timely and accurate monthly, budget, and forecast reporting.
Promote and adhere to the company’s internal methodologies, policies, procedures and standards by consistently maintaining a high quality of work across all allocated functions.
Interpret legislation, government standards and agreements. Provide input/informed commentary, improvement opportunities and areas of risk to management.
Be accountable for the quality of work output from the unit/department through ongoing monitoring and audit process.
Ensure compliance with all statutory and company standards through training and development of staff and promoting by example.
Ensure all administration functions and tasks associated with the position are undertaken and completed in a timely and efficient manner.
Using established training methods and in conjunction with the Training Department, train subordinates to achieve competency in the area identified and within the scope of their position
Participate in training provided by the business.
Comply with established environmentally sustainable measures to not adversely impact the natural fauna, flora, freshwater resources and marine life within the bounds of Simberi Island.
People accountabilities
Ensure staff resources are maximized, and staff members undertake appropriate training and development so they are skilled efficiently to perform allocated duties.
Work with and develop the community through the support of company initiatives.
Are you ready to come and build your future with us?
We need the best people. People who have drive, energy and are genuinely passionate about the work they do and provide a positive impact. Additionally, we need people who see a challenge as an opportunity for growth and value working with others towards a common goal.​
We would love to hear from you if you have​:
Essential
Behaviour consistent with St Barbara’s Values
Bachelor’s Degree in Business Administration, Accounting, Finance, or a related discipline.
CPA qualified or equivalent
Proven experience as a Business Analyst, preferably within the mining, resources, or heavy industry sector.
Strong understanding of mining operations and business processes, including production, maintenance, logistics, and supply chain.
Experience in business process analysis, requirements gathering, and documentation.
Ability to translate business requirements into functional specifications for technical teams.
Strong analytical, financial, and problem-solving skills with attention to detail
Advanced Excel and PowerPoint
Experience working with ERP systems such as Pronto Xi or SAP.

25847.description:
Job Type:
Permanent
About us
K92 Mining Limited are the owners the high-grade Kainantu Gold Mine in Eastern Highlands Province. Since commencing operations in 2016, we have delivered consistent production growth. More importantly, we have contributed significantly to the economy of Papua New Guinea, more than 90% of our employees and contractors are from PNG and our local education and skills development initiatives which include scholarships, traineeships and adult literacy programs continue to bring significant benefit the communities in which we operate.
We are now transforming the operation with a new 1.2 mtpa process plant as well as extensive construction and expansion across site that will see us triple the output from our mine by 2027. In addition to our ongoing production success, we have an extensive exploration programme across our highly prospective tenement, making K92 a great place to build a long-term career.
About the role
Joining our exploration team, the Core Shed Supervisors ensure that Quality Assurance and Quality Control is established on the processing of drill core. This is essential in gathering quality data that is used for both Exploration Purposes and Ore Reserve calculations.
Key Accountabilities
Key accountabilities of this position include.
Manage all drill core technicians ensuring they are working productively.
Train new and existing core technicians so they are following all QAQC protocols.
Ensure all marking up of core is done correctly.
All core is sampled correctly and in a timely manner.
Solve any core block issues or sampling mistakes quickly.
Consistent housekeeping of core shed to make sure it is a safe working environment
Clear communication with the Geologists to help maintain reporting protocols.
Complete all 274’s for the core shed.
Attend all exploration, safety meetings and exploration morning and afternoon meetings.
All data recorded by core shed technicians is done correctly, such as mag sus, XRF and ASD recordings.
Ability to do bulk density readings and RQD.
Work alongside Geologists and core shed technicians. This is a hands-on role.
Perform all other required tasks in consultation with immediate Supervisor.
Maintain safe work standards and practices in accordance with government and company policy.
Perform all roles and responsibilities that support and reflect the company’s mission and core values
About You
To be considered for this position, it is essential that applicants have the following
Minimum Grade ten (10) Certificate.
Minimum of 3-year experience as a core shed supervisor.
Able to understand, read and write Pidgin and English.
Sound communication skills.
Self-Starter and to be able to perform tasks with minimum supervision.
Forklift license.
Well-versed experience in mining safety management.
Of sober habit, a self-starter, very resourceful and with ability to finding solutions.
Excellent oral and written communication skills.
Proficient in computer and e-mail correspondences.
Ability to meet communicated schedules and deadlines.
Strong planning, interpersonal and organizational skills
Current PNG Driver’s license.
Exposure to Emergency Response teams, processes.
Life at K92
K92 is an Equal Opportunity Employer, our commitment is to respect the rights of every individual to work to their highest potential, free from discrimination.  Our values of Collaboration, Accountability, Respect for others, Excellence and Safety are at the core of everything we do, and they are the foundation upon which our success has been built.
Our camp is well managed and provides residents with good, healthy meals made from locally sourced fresh produce as well as internet, cable tv and a gymnasium.
At K92, we want all employees to share in our success, so as well as a competitive salary, employees also participate in our long- and short-term incentive plans, we also provide employees with access to savings incentive programs, medical assistance and the option to salary sacrifice for certain expenses.
In addition to all of this, employees can also access our Wellbeing and employee assistance programs whilst working a friendly roster.
THIS POSITION IS OPEN ONLY TO CANDIDATES WHO HAVE THE RIGHT TO LIVE & WORK IN PNG WITHOUT SPONSORSHIP
Apply

26012.description:
Build a Legacy: Lead transformative projects shaping the future of Port Moresby
Grow Your Career in a dynamic urban environment
Join a passionate team dedicated to a stronger, more vibrant capital.
NC Salary Grade: NC 10
Location:
NCDC City Hall, Waigani, National Capital District
Reporting to:
Snr Waste Management Officer – Waste Disposal
About the National Capital District Commission (NCDC)
The National Capital District Commission (NCDC) is the statutory authority responsible for governing and managing Papua New Guinea’s capital city, Port Moresby.
Unlike other parts of PNG that fall under provincial administrations, Port Moresby sits within a unique administrative area – the National Capital District (NCD) established under its own Act of Parliament. The NCDC is mandated to plan, manage, regulate and shape the capital city on behalf of its residents, communities, and the nation as a whole.
As the gateway to Papua New Guinea, Port Moresby plays a critical national role. The NCDC’s responsibilities extend beyond routine municipal services to include city-wide planning, regulation, infrastructure coordination, social development, and institutional reform in a rapidly growing and complex urban environment.
About the Role
The
Waste Management Officer (WMO)
– Waste Disposal & Illegal Disposal oversees daily waste disposal operations at Baruni Dump and leads NCDC’s response to illegal dumping across the National Capital District. The role involves supervising staff and contractors, monitoring operational risks, ensuring compliance with environmental, health, and safety standards, and coordinating community engagement and enforcement actions to maintain clean and safe communities.
Role Purpose
To ensure the safe, efficient, and compliant management of waste disposal operations, reduce illegal dumping, and improve community cleanliness through proactive monitoring, stakeholder coordination, staff supervision, and continuous operational improvements.
Key Responsibilities
Waste Disposal Oversight:
Supervise daily operations at Baruni Dump, including safe unloading, traffic flow, waste compaction, and contractor activities.
Illegal Dumping Response:
Monitor citywide illegal dumping, plan clean-ups, deploy teams or contractors, document incidents, and support enforcement actions.
Operational Reporting & Compliance:
Maintain accurate records of disposal operations and illegal dumping incidents, submit timely reports, and recommend improvements.
Safety & Environmental Monitoring:
Conduct inspections to identify hazards, ensure PPE use, manage environmental risks, and escalate issues requiring intervention.
Contractor Management:
Coordinate with contractors on attendance, machinery, and operational compliance, monitor performance, and recommend corrective actions.
Staff Supervision & Task Planning:
Support planning, delegation, and guidance to Supervisors and field teams to ensure efficient and compliant operations.
Community & Stakeholder Engagement:
Liaise with residents, local leaders, and internal teams to address concerns, promote responsible waste practices, and support public awareness campaigns.
Service Planning & Continuous Improvement:
Identify operational bottlenecks, safety risks, and service gaps, providing recommendations for improvements.
Procurement Support:
Obtain quotes, prepare purchase requests for operational resources, and monitor resource usage in line with budgets.
Professional Conduct & Development:
Participate in training, capacity-building, and appraisal processes while upholding NCDC’s values of professionalism, integrity, collaboration, and service excellence.
Other Duties:
Perform additional tasks as assigned by managers or the City Manager to support waste management operations.
Education & Qualifications
Minimum:
Bachelor’s degree in Environmental Health, Environmental Science, Waste Management, Public Health, or a related environmental or sustainability discipline.
Preferred:
Additional training or certification in waste operations, public health sanitation, OHS, environmental compliance, or community awareness.
Highly desirable:
Valid Driver’s Licence (minimum Class 3).
Skills & Knowledge
Strong understanding of waste disposal operations, including landfill/dump management, waste flows, compaction, cover procedures, and disposal-site safety requirements.
Knowledge of illegal dumping behaviours, common hotspot patterns, and environmental/public health risks associated with abandoned waste.
Familiarity with NCDC waste management policies, Public Health Act requirements, environmental protection standards, and safety regulations governing disposal-site operations.
Awareness of machinery operations at disposal sites, including loaders, compactors, excavators, and traffic management considerations.
Understanding of environmental risks such as odour, fire, pests, drainage issues, erosion, smoke, and pollution, and appropriate mitigation measures.
Strong operational coordination and site-monitoring skills for supervising disposal-site and illegal dumping activities.
Effective communication and stakeholder engagement skills for interacting with contractors, communities, regulators, and internal NCDC teams.

About the National Capital District Commission (NCDC)
The National Capital District Commission (NCDC) is the statutory authority responsible for governing and managing Papua New Guinea’s capital city, Port Moresby.
Unlike other parts of PNG that fall under provincial administrations, Port Moresby sits within a unique administrative area – the National Capital District (NCD) established under its own Act of Parliament. The NCDC is mandated to plan, manage, regulate and shape the capital city on behalf of its residents, communities, and the nation as a whole.
As the gateway to Papua New Guinea, Port Moresby plays a critical national role. The NCDC’s responsibilities extend beyond routine municipal services to include city-wide planning, regulation, infrastructure coordination, social development, and institutional reform in a rapidly growing and complex urban environment.
About the Role
The
Settlement Development Planner
reports to the Manager – Settlements to Suburbs and leads the preparation and coordination of settlement upgrading layouts and subdivision plans that guide the transition of informal settlements into structured and serviced neighbourhoods. The role ensures that settlement development plans are practical, culturally appropriate, and aligned with the Port Moresby Urban Development Plan, land tenure status, and the sequencing of civil works and service delivery.
The position works closely with the Lands Officer, Mapping Officer, Settlement to Suburbs Project Coordinators, and the Urban Planning Branch to ensure that settlement upgrading designs can be implemented effectively and support secure land tenure, improved access to services, and long-term community sustainability.
Role Purpose
The Settlement Development Planner ensures the preparation and coordination of settlement development plans and subdivision layouts that support the staged delivery of upgrading works. The role provides technically accurate, culturally responsive, and feasible planning outputs that guide the transformation of informal settlements into liveable, safe, and connected urban neighbourhoods. By collaborating with technical officers, project coordinators, and communities, the Planner helps maintain accurate spatial and planning records, supports transparent decision-making, and contributes to sustainable settlement outcomes.
Key Responsibilities
Develop settlement development plans and subdivision layouts that are practical, culturally responsive, and aligned with statutory planning frameworks and Settlements to Suburbs upgrading priorities.
Conduct site assessments to document settlement layout, housing patterns, service access, slope and drainage conditions, flood or erosion risks, and environmental constraints.
Integrate designs for roads, drainage, water, sanitation, pedestrian networks, market spaces, schools, and community facilities in coordination with engineers and service planners.
Develop and assess multiple layout and subdivision options for each settlement, evaluating land capacity, topography, community needs, and service delivery feasibility before confirming final plans.
Incorporate space for pedestrian movement, communal areas, market activity, schools, clinics, and cultural gathering spaces to support liveable neighbourhood function.
Ensure settlement layouts support safe mobility, climate resilience, equitable land allocation, social inclusion, and long-term neighbourhood integration.
Work closely with the Urban Planning Branch to ensure SDPs align with the Port Moresby Urban Development Plan, zoning intentions, and long-term urban structure plans.
Coordinate with the Lands Officer and Mapping Officer to ensure subdivision layouts reflect verified land tenure, boundaries, and accurate spatial data.
Provide planning inputs and layout guidance to S2S Project Coordinators to support sequencing and construction works.
Coordinate with the Social Development Branch to ensure settlement layouts respect community patterns of use, cultural spaces, and social support needs.
Present draft settlement layouts to community leaders, ILGs, and residents to collect input and support shared understanding of proposed changes.
Support awareness sessions and planning consultations conducted with community social development teams and Project Coordinators.
Maintain up-to-date spatial datasets, structure plans, population estimates, and service needs for each settlement plan.
Prepare planning reports, visual layouts, presentations, and supporting documentation for internal review and external reporting.
Prepare layout documentation required for submission to statutory planning or subdivision approval processes, where applicable.
Ensure settlement plans comply with Physical Planning Act requirements, subdivision and building standards, NCDC planning policies, and city development guidelines.
Prepare planning-related cost estimates and technical inputs (e.g., surveys, pegging, consultation support, and subdivision drafting fees) to assist the Manager and Project Coordinators in preparing budgets and procurement requests.
Undertake additional tasks as assigned by the Manager – Urban Projects.
Education & Qualifications
Minimum:
Diploma in Urban Planning, Land Administration, Architecture, Civil Engineering, or a related discipline from a recognised tertiary institution.
Preferred:
Bachelor’s degree in Urban Planning, Geography, or Development Studies. Additional certification in community development, project management, or GIS is an advantage.
Advantage: Current valid drivers license.
Skills & Knowledge
Understanding of settlement planning, subdivision layout design, and neighbourhood development principles.
Familiarity with PNG land tenure systems and relevant legislation (Physical Planning Act, Land Act, Survey Act).
Knowledge of infrastructure service planning (roads, drainage, water, sanitation, public facilities) in settlement contexts.
Awareness of participatory planning methods and culturally appropriate community engagement practices.
Understanding of the Settlements to Suburbs Program and the Port Moresby Urban Development Plan.
Ability to prepare layout plans, analyse spatial data, and translate field observations into planning outputs.
Clear communication and presentation skills to explain planning options to communities and stakeholders.
Ability to facilitate, not negotiate, land and settlement planning discussions respectfully.
Strong organisational and time management skills to manage multiple planning tasks under deadlines.
Proficiency in Microsoft Office, with exposure to GIS or mapping software preferred.
Cultural sensitivity, integrity, and professionalism when working with communities and landowners.
Demonstrated commitment to NCDC’s values and improving settlement living conditions.
Work Experience
Minimum of three (3) years’ experience in urban planning, settlement upgrading, land administration, or related project work.
Experience in community consultation and preparing planning layouts or subdivision plans is desirable.
Experience liaising with government agencies, planning authorities, technical consultants, and customary landowner groups is an advantage.
Why Join NCDC?
This role offers a unique opportunity to influence how data shapes the future of Papua New Guinea’s capital city. You will work at the centre of urban development, infrastructure planning, and service delivery—contributing to projects that leave a lasting legacy for Port Moresby.
Ready to Make an Impact?

Open to Port Moresby residents only.
Due to volume of candidates, only short-listed candidates will be contacted regarding applicant progress.
Applications are assessed on merit, capability, and alignment with NCDC’s values and service mandate.
Be part of the team shaping the future of Port Moresby — apply today.

Our vision is to grow sustainably and create enduring, positive impacts for the people and communities touched by our operations.
Now is an exciting time for our business and for our people. We’re going through a period of significant change and are gaining momentum in transforming our business. We’re looking for people who are ready to grow through opportunity and build a bright future with us.​​

Relief Travel Supervisor

Reporting to the Travel Superintendent, the Travel Supervisor is primarily responsible for supervising the management of Travel and Hotel Accommodation Bookings which is the control source for making travel arrangements, enforcing the company travel policy, and helping with the administration of domestic and international travel bookings and company charter.

Issuing purchase orders to airflight companies and hotels.

Prepare and filing of all flight related manifests, consignment notes and flight documentation.
Preparation and distribution of all flight and charter schedules.
Responsible for transporting staff to and from Mine and Airport.
Loading/unloading, pick up and transport of all personnel, baggage, and freight to and from the Simberi accommodation camp and Simberi airstrip.
All other travel and accommodation related work as directed.
Scheduling accountabilities
Demonstrated supervisory/leadership capacity and continuous improvement mindset.
Management reporting
The ability to meet safety targets and requirements.
Actively participate and promote a safe working environment.
Actively participate in departmental safety meetings and display a safe attitude.
Competent, accurate and time-based record keeping.
Punctual attendance for all rostered shifts.
People accountabilities
Using established training methods and in conjunction with the Training Department train subordinates to achieve competency in the area identified and within the scope of their position.
Participate in training provided by the business.

We need the best people. People who have the drive, energy and are genuinely passionate about the work they do and provide a positive impact. Additionally, we need people who see a challenge as an opportunity for growth and value working with others towards a common goal.​

Essential
Behaviour consistent with St Barbara’s Values
Previous experience working in the mining industry.
Previous experience in the travel industry.
Must have current Driver’s Licence.
Working knowledge of travel policies and procedures.
Aircraft handling/loading/refuelling procedures.
Excellent PC skills including word processing, spreadsheet applications and internet functions.
Excellent organization, planning and supervisory skills.
Excellent interpersonal skills including oral and written communication.
Desirable
Physically fit and healthy.
Prepared to work outside normal hours as required.
Ability to work under minimal supervision.

Grow Your Career in a dynamic urban environment.
Join a passionate team dedicated to a stronger, more vibrant capital.

NC.10

NCDC City Hall, Waigani, National Capital District

Manager – Urban Planning
About the National Capital District Commission (NCDC)
The National Capital District Commission (NCDC) is the statutory authority responsible for governing and managing Papua New Guinea’s capital city, Port Moresby.
Unlike other parts of PNG that fall under provincial administrations, Port Moresby sits within a unique administrative area – the National Capital District (NCD) established under its own Act of Parliament. The NCDC is mandated to plan, manage, regulate and shape the capital city on behalf of its residents, communities, and the nation as a whole.
As the gateway to Papua New Guinea, Port Moresby plays a critical national role. The NCDC’s responsibilities extend beyond routine municipal services to include city-wide planning, regulation, infrastructure coordination, social development, and institutional reform in a rapidly growing and complex urban environment.
About the Role
The
Customary Lands Officer
supports traditional landowning groups within the National Capital District to document, protect, and manage their customary land interests in line with legislation and urban development priorities. The role acts as NCDC’s key liaison on customary land matters, working with landowners, government agencies, and statutory bodies to support tenure recognition, boundary verification, and dispute resolution.
Role Purpose
The purpose of the Customary Lands Officer is to ensure customary land interests are accurately identified and appropriately considered in planning and development processes. Through community engagement, documentation, and advisory support, the role promotes culturally respectful land governance, legal compliance, and inclusive urban development across Port Moresby.
Key Responsibilities
Verify and document customary land boundaries, ownership claims, and land use through field engagement and consultation.
Liaise with traditional landowners, DLPP, statutory bodies, and internal NCDC branches to support tenure recognition, planning decisions, and dispute resolution.
Provide advisory input, reports, and mapping information to inform development proposals, infrastructure planning, and land governance.
Education & Qualifications
Minimum: Diploma in Land Administration, Customary Land Studies, Urban and Regional Planning, or a related field, supported by relevant training in land management, dispute resolution, or community engagement.
Preferred: Bachelor in Land Management, Geography, Urban Planning, or Customary Land Tenure from a recognised institution.
Required: Valid PNG driver’s licence
Preferred: Eligible for membership with a recognised professional body (e.g., PNG Institute of Planners, Institute of Surveyors PNG, or equivalent).
Skills & Knowledge
Knowledge of customary land systems, traditional land ownership structures, and urbanisation impacts on customary land within the National Capital District
.
Familiarity with the
Land Act (1996)
,
Physical Planning Act (1989 & 2001)
,
Survey Act (1969)
,
NCDC Act (2001)
, and willingness to gain deeper understanding of customary land rights and dispute processes.
Understanding of formal lease conversion pathways and issues surrounding informal settlements on customary land.
Awareness of inter-agency roles and procedures involving DLPP, the Surveyor General’s Office, and community dispute mechanisms.
Knowledge of ethical and culturally sensitive practices when working with traditional landowners and clan-based landholding systems.
Customary Land Practice: Ability to document traditional land claims, support verification of landowner identities, and assist in resolving encroachment or land use disputes.
Community Engagement: Skilled in communicating respectfully with landowners, clan leaders, and community groups, and representing NCDC in culturally appropriate ways.
Documentation and Records: Competent in preparing tenure documentation, land history records, and correspondence relating to customary land.
Stakeholder Coordination:Strong liaison skills with DLPP, legal services, civil society partners, and internal NCDC teams.
Technical Proficiency: Proficient in Microsoft Office and capable of using basic GIS tools or mapping software.
Ethical Standards and Reliability: Demonstrated integrity, discretion, and commitment to responsible public sector land management.
Work Experience
Minimum of 3 years’ experience in customary land matters, community-based land management, or land dispute mediation
Experience working with or alongside DLPP, surveyors, or planning authorities in documenting or verifying land tenure.
Prior involvement in community awareness or advisory activities related to land rights, leasing options, or informal settlement impacts.
Experience supporting urban planning or development programs through customary land documentation or stakeholder engagement.
Why Join NCDC?
This role offers a unique opportunity to influence how data shapes the future of Papua New Guinea’s capital city. You will work at the centre of urban development, infrastructure planning, and service delivery—contributing to projects that leave a lasting legacy for Port Moresby.
Ready to Make an Impact?
If you are passionate about data-driven decision-making and city transformation, we encourage you to apply.
How to Apply
Interested candidates are encouraged to:
Review the available roles and position requirements
Prepare to upload relevant supporting documentation
Cover Letter
Up-to-date CV, include in the one file along with your CV: copies of educational qualifications and a copy of a valid driver's licence (if applicable)
Click on the "APPLY NOW" button and submit an application through the Peopleconnexion PNG application portal.
Open to Port Moresby residents only.
Due to volume of candidates, only short-listed candidates will be contacted regarding applicant progress.
Applications are assessed on merit, capability, and alignment with NCDC’s values and service mandate.
Be part of the team shaping the future of Port Moresby — apply today.
Apply

26184.description:
Terms of Reference (ToR)
Consultancy to Develop a Child Safeguarding Policy and Child-Friendly Version for the National Office of Child and Family Services (NOCFS), Papua New Guinea
Project:
Together for Safe Families
Organization:
Save the Children in Papua New Guinea
Location:
Port Moresby
Duration:
40 days over a period of five months
Background
Save the Children is implementing the
Together for Safe Families
project in Papua New Guinea, which aims to reduce violence against children by strengthening families, challenging harmful gender and social norms, empowering children, and improving child protection systems.
The project supports the Government of Papua New Guinea in strengthening the child protection system at provincial and national levels, including improvements to policy and legal frameworks and institutional capacity.
As part of this commitment, Save the Children will provide technical support to the
National Office of Child and Family Services (NOCFS)
to develop a comprehensive
Child Safeguarding Policy
. This policy will ensure that children are protected from abuse, neglect, exploitation, and harm when engaging with NOCFS staff and services. The policy will operationalize safeguarding standards within NOCFS to ensure that all staff, contractors, volunteers, and partners working with children uphold child-safe practices consistent with PNG’s legal framework. The policy will contribute to improving child protection services and strengthening institutional accountability.
In addition, a
child-friendly version
of the policy will be developed to ensure children understand their rights, available reporting mechanisms, and the responsibilities of adults working with them.
Purpose of the Consultancy
The purpose of this consultancy is to:
Develop a comprehensive Child Safeguarding Policy for NOCFS aligned with Lukautim Pikinini Act and other relevant national laws, international standards, and best practices.
Ensure meaningful consultation with key stakeholders, including children, to help guide the development of this policy
Develop a child-friendly version of the (same) safeguarding policy.
Facilitate validation of the final policy and work with the NOCFS to develop a dissemination plan for the final policy (and child-friendly version).
Scope of Work
The consultant will undertake the following tasks:
3.1 Review and Analysis
Review existing national laws, policies, and regulations related to child protection and safeguarding in Papua New Guinea.
Review relevant international frameworks and standards.
Map safeguarding requirements under the Lukautim Pikinini Act to NOCFS operational mandates.
Identify gaps between current NOCFS practices and statutory child protection obligations.
Ensure the safeguarding policy complements statutory child protection responsibilities under the Act.
Clarify reporting obligations consistent with national referral pathways and legal requirements.
Align procedures with PNG’s existing case management and child welfare systems.
3.2 Stakeholder Engagement
Identify and engage key stakeholders including:
Relevant government agencies
NGOs and civil society organizations
Child protection experts, academic institutions
Development partners
Facilitate structured consultations to gather inputs and ensure the policy reflects local realities and institutional capacity.
Facilitate safe and ethical consultations with children to gather age-appropriate inputs into policy development.
3.3 Policy Development
Develop a comprehensive Child Safeguarding Policy including, but not limited to:
Policy statement and guiding principles
Definitions and scope
Code of conduct
Prevention measures (safe recruitment, background checks, staff training, supervision)
Reporting mechanisms and complaint procedures
Response protocols and case management guidance
Confidentiality and data protection
Risk assessment and mitigation measures
Roles and responsibilities
Monitoring and accountability mechanisms
Alignment with Papua New Guinea’s legal and regulatory frameworks
3.4 Validation and Finalization
Facilitate validation workshop(s) with stakeholders.
Incorporate feedback and finalize the policy.
Ensure the policy is practical, implementable, and context appropriate.
3.5 Child-Friendly Version
Develop an accessible, age-appropriate child-friendly version of the safeguarding policy.
Use simple language and culturally appropriate examples.
Ensure clarity on:
Children’s rights
Expected behaviour of adults
How and where children can report concerns
Deliverables
The consultant will deliver:
Inception report (methodology, timeline, stakeholder mapping)
Summary of stakeholder consultation findings
Draft Child Safeguarding Policy
Validation workshop report
Final Child Safeguarding Policy
Child-Friendly Version of the Policy
Required Qualifications and Experience
The consultant should have:
Advanced degree in Child Protection, Social Work, Law, Public Policy, International Development, or related field.
Minimum 7–10 years of experience in child protection or safeguarding or code of conduct policy development.
Demonstrated experience developing safeguarding and/or protection policies for government or large institutions is preferred.
Strong knowledge of Papua New Guinea’s child protection legal and policy environment.
Experience conducting participatory consultations, including with children.
Strong facilitation and drafting skills.
Experience developing child-friendly materials.
Excellent written and spoken English.
Ethical Considerations
The consultant must:
Adhere to Save the Children’s Child Safeguarding Policy and Code of Conduct.
Ensure safe and ethical engagement of children.
Maintain confidentiality of all sensitive information.
Ensure informed consent and child-appropriate safeguarding protocols during consultations.
Reporting and Supervision
The consultant will report to the Protection Manager, Save the Children in Papua New Guinea. Technical oversight will be provided jointly by Save the Children and NOCFS.
Application Process
Interested consultants should submit:
Technical proposal (methodology and workplan)
Financial proposal
CV(s)
Samples of previous policy work
Contact details of three professional referees
Email Applications To:
[email protected]
Apply

About us
K92 Mining Limited are the owners the high-grade Kainantu Gold Mine in Eastern Highlands Province. Since commencing operations in 2016, we have delivered consistent production growth. More importantly, we have contributed significantly to the economy of Papua New Guinea, more than 90% of our employees and contractors are from PNG and our local education and skills development initiatives which include scholarships, traineeships and adult literacy programs continue to bring significant benefit the communities in which we operate.

In addition to our ongoing production success, we have an extensive exploration programme across our highly prospective tenement, making K92 a great place to build a long-term career.

Joining our Operational Services maintenance team, this role is responsible for the implementation and maintenance of mine power supply and distribution system for all electrical equipment on the mine and on our exploration sites in Kainantu. In addition, this position will also play an important role in the training of trades assistants.

Inspect, isolate, and repair electrical malfunctions using various hand and power tools.
Ensure that alarms and emergency electrical systems onsite are always operational.
Direct and train subordinates to install, maintain or repair electrical wiring, equipment, and machines.
Ensure and maintain safe work standards and practices in accordance with mine safety regulations for all tasks performed.

To be considered for this role, it is essential that you have a NATTB Trade Certificate as well a current electrical license. You will also need to demonstrate experience in the installation and maintenance of power distribution systems, transformers, motor control centres and starters. Five (5) years’ experience working in a mining environment.
You must have a High Voltage switching ticket.
You must have a wide experience in installation and maintenance of Low and High Voltage transfers and starters.
Must be a self-starter and very resourceful with ability to find solutions to problems to ensure the equipment availability is high.
Be flexible and adaptable to the needs of the business and ability to work harmoniously as part of the team.

Our people are the heart of our success, bringing exceptional skill, integrity, and dedication to everything we do as an organization and we’re dedicated to creating a workplace where everyone can thrive.
About Lihir
Our Lihir Operation, located on the beautiful island of Niolam, approximately 800km north of Papua New Guinea's capital, Port Moresby, is one of the world’s largest gold mines. Set within a geothermically active, extinct volcanic crater, Lihir operates an open-pit mine producing refractory ore, which undergoes pressure oxidation and conventional leaching to recover gold. Our workforce includes both residential and commute rosters, creating a diverse and dynamic team. Lihir offers a range of recreational facilities, including a gym, sports club, restaurant, bar, swimming pool, tennis and squash courts, and a 9-hole golf course. For those who enjoy the outdoors, the Lihir fishing and boating clubs provide access to pristine waters and beaches, while our onsite deli and café serve fresh local and imported produce, barista-made coffee, and freshly baked goods.
We are proud to work closely with the local Lihirian community and value its vibrant culture. Through initiatives like our School to Mine program, we offer meaningful employment, training, and development opportunities for Lihirian men and women, as well as scholarships and vocational apprenticeships. We also partner with the New Ireland Province to ensure economic benefits flow directly to the community, strengthening our commitment to sustainable development and positive local impact.
Your Impact
As a Technician – Geothermal Operations, you will play a vital role in supporting Lihir’s geothermal monitoring and safety systems. Your work ensures accurate data collection, reliable operation of geothermal systems or similar geotechnical operational systems, and strong hazard awareness across the open pit. By applying your technical skills, attention to detail, and commitment to safety, you’ll help maintain safe mining conditions, support geothermal project delivery, and contribute to the ongoing development of geothermal monitoring across operational teams.
As part of our team, you will
Ensure full compliance with all HSE requirements, policies, and Fitness for Work standards.
Complete HSE tasks only when hazards, risks, and controls are clearly understood and agreed with your Supervisor.
Work constructively within a diverse team and take accountability for your own development and performance.
Lead the installation and data collection of geothermal monitoring systems in the open pit.
Contribute to the execution of mine geothermal projects and support geothermal hazard training for operational and technical teams.
Conduct preventative maintenance inspections on geothermal equipment, including steam relief wells.
Identify cost‑saving opportunities and report any cost wastage within your area of responsibility.
Prerequisites for your success in this role
Essential
Grade 12 education.
PNG Class 6 Driver’s Licence.
More than 1 year of experience in a mining or technical role.
Strong analytical, troubleshooting, and problem‑solving skills.
Ability to work safely and effectively in a multicultural team.
Competency in Microsoft Word and Excel.
Strong communication, interpersonal, and active listening skills.
High attention to detail, good time management, and the ability to work independently when required.
Desirable
Diploma in IT Networking, Electronics, Instrumentation, or a similar technical field.
Experience with data and software networking, system communications, and technical reporting.
Familiarity with geothermal or geotechnical monitoring systems.
Your work environment
This position is based at the Lihir Gold Operation on a
22:20 FIFO roster – days only
. You’ll be part of a small, supportive team within Mine Technical Services, working closely with the Supervisor – Geothermal Systems.
The role offers hands‑on fieldwork, exposure to geothermal monitoring technologies, and clear development pathways, including opportunities to progress into supervisory or geotechnical operations roles. You’ll thrive in an environment that values safety, teamwork, continuous learning, and technical excellence.
Our FIFO employees stay in a secure and comfortable camp, in an ensuited and airconditioned room equipped with mini fridge, TV and Wi-Fi. A variety of healthy meal options are catered for at our mess; and the wet mess provides a relaxed social setting where employees can unwind with a game of pool or darts.
Why Join Newmont
At Newmont, our commitment to diversity and inclusion ensures that everyone can work to their full potential, free from discrimination, while respecting the cultures, religions, and governance of the regions in which we operate. Guided by our values of Safety, Integrity, Sustainability, Responsibility, and Inclusion, our Lihir team – 90% of which are Papua New Guinean – is dedicated to creating a culturally rich and supportive environment where meaningful, long-term connections can be formed within the industry.
We believe in the strength of our people and the positive impact we can create together. Newmont employees are rewarded with a competitive salary, flexible packaging options, and programs that recognize those who go above and beyond. We know no candidate meets every qualification listed, so if you share our values and feel you can make a meaningful contribution, we encourage you to apply – we’d love to hear from you!

26306.description:
Don’t come for an easy career. Stay for a rewarding one.
Santos is a global energy company committed to increasingly cleaner energy and fuels production, with operations across Australia, Papua New Guinea, Timor-Leste and North America.
We are currently PNG’s largest single investor and most active explorer, operating all the country’s producing oil fields and holding an extensive appraisal and exploration portfolio. Our aspirations and strategies reflect our genuine commitment to making a meaningful contribution to the lives of Papua New Guineans.
At Santos, our commitment is to be a global leader in the transition to cleaner energy and clean fuels, by helping the world decarbonise to reach net-zero emissions in an affordable and sustainable way.
Santos is one of Australia’s biggest domestic gas supplier, a leading Asia Pacific LNG supplier and is committed to supplying the critical fuels such as oil and gas in a more sustainable way through decarbonising projects such as the Moomba CCS project.
For more than 65 years, Santos has been working in partnership with local communities, providing local jobs and business opportunities, safely and sustainably developing its natural gas resources, and powering industries and households.
What you’ll do:
Based in Iagifu Ridge on a 28 day on/ 28 day off roster, the Site Manager is the single point of accountability for all on-site activities, from early works through to Ready for Operations (RFO), handover, punch list close-out, and project demobilisation.
This role drives on-site execution, sets priorities where demands conflict, and makes the final call on trade-offs between facilities, pipelines, and resources. Working with the Senior Manager APF Projects, the Project Leadership Team, and Santos Base Business, the Site Manager delivers the outcomes that determine project success.
This is a 2-year Max Term Contract opportunity. We are open to receiving expatriate applicants (Point of Hire Brisbane) as well as PNG National applicants.
Key Responsibilities:
Establish and lead a strong project safety culture on site, including visible leadership, proactive reporting, site safety audits, incident initiation and participation in investigations.
Act as Person in Charge (PIC) for the Project, accountable for all site activities and emergency response management.
Oversee and execute site construction plans from early works through to completion and handover.
Provide direction to the Construction Lead, Pipeline and Construction Lead Facilities where priorities conflict, maintaining a whole project perspective.
Ensure all construction and execution activities comply with regulatory, corporate and functional requirements.
Ensure core project resources (HSS, Quality and others) are effectively allocated across site activities.
Maintain accountability for site team resourcing and competency through the Execute Phase.
Manage site interfaces with Santos base operations, ensuring appropriate shared services support.
Interface with concurrent on-site projects to assess and manage impacts arising from changing business priorities.
Partner with field-based Project Controls to ensure accurate cost and progress reporting, including forecast performance.
Identify and address communication gaps or stakeholder misalignment at site.
Develop and lead an integrated site team capable of executing scope, making sound decisions and resolving conflict effectively.
What you’ll bring:
Extensive experience in construction and construction management roles.
Experience with brownfield hydrocarbon projects.
Proven track record delivering in complex, challenging, and remote environments.
Experience in remote, developing countries and wet tropics environments.
Exceptional leadership, team management, conflict resolution, and coaching/mentoring skills.
Highly effective communication, coordination, and collaboration abilities, with a talent for building strong working relationships.
Solid technical understanding of the oil and gas value chain.
Knowledge of standards and codes for hydrocarbon infrastructure construction in PNG.
Ability to implement project strategy while maintaining quality control and HSES compliance.
Strong commercial acumen and sound business judgment regarding people, projects, and processes.
Delivery-focused, with a collaborative “team player” mindset.
Innovative problem-solving skills, especially in group or high-pressure environments.
Tertiary qualification in engineering, project management, or a related discipline.
PNG project construction execution experience desirable.
Construction or safety management certifications desirable.
What you’ll get:
Here, you’ll be amongst high-calibre people and get to work on industry-leading projects. We don’t shy away from solving tough problems at pace. We like it that way. You can expect to be challenged and supported; to learn and grow.
At Santos, we’re committed to creating a workplace where everyone can thrive. This means a place that is safe; where you are valued and respected, and your contribution is recognised and appreciated. Join us, and you’ll play a role in this too.
Each of our sites offer access to specific amenities that aim to create the best possible benefits to your health, wellbeing and performance.
What you’re part of:
Everywhere you turn you will be a part of a team who are coming together to contribute to our single uniting purpose - to provide reliable and affordable energy to help create a better world for everyone And because it’s not only what you do, but how you do it, you will also contribute to improving the living standards of the communities where we operate, building enduring and respectful relationships that serve a generation. It’s about each of us, and all of us – together.
How to Apply
Applications must be submitted via the online recruitment system before
COB 23rd March 2026.
Potential Scams
There are a number of fake adverts that are impersonating Santos Limited, in these instances you will receive an e-mail from a generic e-mail address. We do not make offers without interviews or due diligence taking place. You will know if an advert is genuine if you are directed to the Santos company careers page to apply which is
https://recruitment.santos.com/
Apply

26303.description:
Papua New Guinea University of Natural Resources and Environment (PNGUNRE)
About the University
The Papua New Guinea University of Natural Resources and Environment (PNGUNRE) is a specialised national institution mandated to advance education, research, innovation, and community engagement in sustainable agriculture, natural resource management, environmental stewardship, and applied development disciplines.
PNGUNRE operates across three campuses:
Vudal Main Campus (East New Britain Province) – home to core teaching and research programs
Takubar Campus (Kokopo) – host of Postgraduate Programs and the Department of Business & Economics
Popondetta Campus (Oro Province) – focused on agricultural training and community development initiatives
The University emphasises practice-oriented teaching, field-based learning, and strong industry collaboration, producing graduates who are work-ready and capable of contributing meaningfully to sustainable development and climate-resilient outcomes across Papua New Guinea.
About the Role
PNGUNRE invites applications from suitably qualified and motivated candidates for appointment as
Tutor (Technical Instructor – Renewable Energy & Environmental Engineering)
within the Department of Renewable Energy & Environmental Engineering, School of Environment and Climate Change (SECC).
This position supports the delivery of tutorials, laboratory sessions, and applied practical learning in Renewable Energy and Environmental Engineering programs. The role contributes to undergraduate teaching, laboratory-based instruction, applied research support, and industry- and community-linked activities aligned with PNGUNRE’s mandate in renewable energy development, environmental sustainability, and climate change response.
The successful appointee will work under the direction of a Lecturer and report to the Head of Department, Renewable Energy & Environmental Engineering.
Key Responsibilities
Assist Lecturers in the preparation and delivery of tutorials, laboratory sessions, and practical classes in Renewable Energy and Environmental Engineering.
Plan, prepare, and support engineering laboratories and applied practical classes to enhance student learning outcomes.
Provide technical assistance to students during laboratory work, practical assessments, and applied learning activities.
Assist in setting assessment tasks, marking scripts, and submission of student results in accordance with university procedures.
Support academic staff in applied research activities, including data collection, laboratory work, and research implementation.
Contribute to the preparation of teaching and learning materials and laboratory manuals.
Participate in short courses, workshops, seminars, and industry or community engagement activities facilitated by the Department.
Attend departmental, school, and University meetings, seminars, and training as required.
Liaise with internal and external stakeholders on technical and instructional matters, as directed by the Head of Department.
Ensure compliance with university quality assurance standards, academic regulations, and administrative protocols.
Undertake other duties as reasonably directed by the Head of Department and Dean, School of Environment and Climate Change.
Qualifications, Experience & Competency Profile
Bachelor’s degree from a recognised university in Renewable Energy, Electrical Engineering, Environmental Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, or a closely related discipline.
A master’s degree in a relevant field is an advantage.
Broad technical knowledge of renewable energy systems, environmental engineering applications, and climate-related technologies.
Demonstrated ability to support laboratory-based teaching and practical instruction in undergraduate engineering programs.
Familiarity with Life Cycle Assessment software, AutoCAD, and Building Information Modelling (BIM) is desirable.
Ability to plan, organise, and implement engineering laboratory and practical classes.
Competency in Microsoft Office applications and basic ICT systems used in academic environments.
Strong written and oral communication skills and the ability to work effectively with students, academic staff, and external partners.
Good interpersonal skills, professional presentation, and a collaborative team approach.
Ability to manage workload pressures during peak academic periods.
High standards of professionalism, integrity, ethical conduct, and commitment to PNGUNRE values.
Salary Range
Tutor (Technical Instructor)
K36,288.00 – K55,632.00
(plus applicable allowances and benefits)
Why Join PNGUNRE?
This role offers an opportunity to contribute directly to the development of practically skilled, industry-ready graduates in renewable energy and environmental engineering—key priority areas for Papua New Guinea’s sustainable development and climate resilience agenda. PNGUNRE provides a supportive applied learning environment with strong emphasis on laboratory work, field-based training, and community engagement.
Application Details
Interested applicants should submit:
A cover letter addressing teaching, practical, and technical experience
A detailed Curriculum Vitae
Certified copies of academic qualifications
Names and contact details of three (3) referees
Applications must be addressed to:
The Manager – Human Resources
Papua New Guinea University of Natural Resources and Environment
Vudal Campus, East New Britain Province
Email:
[email protected]
Closing Date: 20 March 2026
PNGUNRE is an equal opportunity employer and encourages applications from suitably qualified candidates.
Apply

Papua New Guinea University of Natural Resources and Environment (PNGUNRE)
About the University
The Papua New Guinea University of Natural Resources and Environment (PNGUNRE) is a specialised national institution mandated to advance education, research, innovation, and community engagement in sustainable agriculture, natural resource management, environmental stewardship, and applied development disciplines.
PNGUNRE operates across three campuses:
Vudal Main Campus (East New Britain Province) – core teaching and research programs
Takubar Campus (Kokopo) – postgraduate programs and business-related disciplines
Popondetta Campus (Oro Province) – agricultural training and community development initiatives
The University places strong emphasis on practice-oriented teaching, field-based learning, applied research, and partnerships with government, industry, and communities, producing graduates equipped to address Papua New Guinea’s climate, environmental, and development challenges.
About the Role
PNGUNRE invites applications from early-career academics and professionals with capability in Climate Change, Health, and Development for appointment
as Tutor (Technical Instructor)
within the Department of Climate Change, Health and Development, School of Environment & Climate Change.
This position is designed as an academic career-pathway role, supporting progression to Lecturer I and Lecturer II subject to performance, qualifications, and research development.
The role is based at Vudal Campus with responsibilities extending to field sites and community locations across East New Britain Province, including Upper Baining areas and surrounding island communities such as the Duke of York Islands.
The appointment supports the University’s strategic focus on applied climate change education, community engagement, and research-informed teaching, while building the candidate’s academic, research, and professional scholarship profile.
Key Responsibilities
Support the delivery of undergraduate courses in Climate Change, Climate Adaptation and Mitigation, Health and Development, and related environmental disciplines, using applied and outcomes-based teaching approaches.
Facilitate tutorials, practical sessions, and field-based learning activities, including community-focused engagement and applied case studies.

26300.description:
Papua New Guinea University of Natural Resources and Environment (PNGUNRE)
About the University
The Papua New Guinea University of Natural Resources and Environment (PNGUNRE) is a specialised national institution mandated to advance education, research, innovation, and community engagement in sustainable agriculture, natural resource management, environmental stewardship, and applied development disciplines.
PNGUNRE operates across three campuses:
Vudal Main Campus (East New Britain Province) – core teaching and research programs
Takubar Campus (Kokopo) – postgraduate programs and business-related disciplines
Popondetta Campus (Oro Province) – agricultural training and community development
The University emphasises practice-oriented teaching, field-based learning, applied research, and strong engagement with government, industry, and communities, producing graduates capable of addressing Papua New Guinea’s environmental and climate challenges.
About the Role
PNGUNRE invites applications from academics with demonstrated expertise in
Climate Change and Environmental Sciences
for appointment as Lecturer I or Lecturer II within the Department of Climate Change, School of Environment & Climate Change.
The role is based at Vudal Campus with responsibilities extending to field sites and community locations across East New Britain Province. The appointment places strong emphasis on climate science, applied research, teaching excellence, and community and policy engagement, aligned with national climate priorities and international environmental frameworks.
The successful appointee will contribute to teaching, research, professional scholarship, and applied services supporting climate resilience, environmental management, and sustainable development.
Key Responsibilities
Deliver undergraduate and postgraduate courses in Climate Change, Environmental Science, Natural Resource Management, and related disciplines, using outcomes-based and applied teaching approaches.
Design and deliver field-based teaching, community engagement activities, and applied learning experiences across East New Britain Province and relevant locations.
Supervise student research projects and contribute to academic scholarship in climate change, environmental systems, and sustainable development.
Conduct and publish applied and scholarly research in areas such as climate change impacts, ecological assessment, environmental health, renewable energy, or climate adaptation.
Contribute to curriculum development, course coordination, and continuous quality improvement in accordance with university academic standards.
Support professional and policy-oriented activities, including short courses, workshops, seminars, and stakeholder forums.
Build and maintain effective working relationships with government agencies, research institutions, NGOs, and community organisations.
Participate in departmental, school, and university committees and academic governance processes.
Mentor junior academic staff, tutors, and technical personnel.
Undertake other academic and administrative duties as directed by the Head of Department.
Qualifications, Experience & Competency Profile
Master’s degree (MA, MPhil, MSc) or PhD in Climate Change, Environmental Science, Environmental Studies, Natural Resource Management, Environmental Health, Applied Sciences, Social Sciences, or a closely related discipline from a recognised university.
Candidates with a PhD and 2–5 years of relevant postdoctoral, industry, government, or NGO experience are strongly encouraged to apply.
Demonstrated capability to teach and contribute academically at Lecturers I or II level.
Strong understanding of climate change science, environmental systems, and sustainable development challenges relevant to Papua New Guinea and the Pacific region.
Experience conducting applied research, fieldwork, or community-based environmental projects.
Ability to contribute to quality assurance, academic governance, and curriculum development.
Competence in research methods, data analysis, and reporting; experience with statistical or analytical tools is desirable.
Strong written and oral communication skills, with the ability to prepare reports and present findings to diverse audiences.
High standards of professionalism, ethical conduct, resilience, and commitment to community and environmental outcomes.

Lecturer I / Lecturer II
K48,382.26 – K59,132.71
(plus applicable allowances and benefits)

This role offers a unique opportunity to contribute directly to climate change education, research, and community impact in Papua New Guinea. PNGUNRE provides a collaborative academic environment that values field-based science, applied policy engagement, and solutions-oriented research addressing national and regional environmental priorities.
